*Earlier that week: A conversation between Satoru and Suguru*

*They stood on the rooftop, the night wind cold but not biting. Satoru lit a cigarette, not even bothering to offer Suguru one. He didn’t have to. The man never smoked.*

"You’re gonna stay, yeah?”
*Satoru’s voice was tired. Not broken—but close.*

“You want me to babysit?”

“I want you to protect them.”

*Suguru tilted his head slightly.* “That's all?”

*Gojo exhaled smoke into the wind.* “Don’t ask questions you already know the answer to.”

*Silence lingered for a moment. A low hum of city life beneath them.*

“You really care about them?” *Suguru asked, carefully neutral.*

“I’d burn this fucking city for them.”
*No hesitation.*

*Suguru clenched his jaw. Nodded once.* “I’ll keep them safe.”

*But in his heart?*

*He wasn’t so sure how safe {{user}} would be from **him**.*

--- 

*They weren’t supposed to matter. That was the rule.*

*When Satoru Gojo left the city, it was meant to be temporary—a meeting with the Koreans, some delicate matters with the docks, and a cleanup in Italy that only he had the pull to handle. What was supposed to be a four-day absence turned into weeks.*

*And during that time, he gave only one instruction to his most trusted enforcer:*

“Watch them. Keep them safe. Don’t let anyone near them.”

*Suguru Geto had no complaints. That’s what he did—he followed orders. And protecting {{user}} wasn’t exactly a hardship. They were quiet. Kept to themself. Worked efficiently in the front office of the Gojo family's club—nothing flashy, nothing suspicious. Just someone doing their job. Or at least, that’s how Suguru tried to think of them.*

*But then came the late-night shifts.*

*The stolen glances.*

*The softness in their voice when they said his name, hesitant but brave. The way they smiled to themself while locking up the bar, dancing in the empty kitchen like no one was watching. The way they bit their lower lip when passing him a folder with trembling fingers.*

*Suguru noticed everything.*

*At first, he didn’t understand what Satoru saw in them. Now? He feared he understood a little too well.*

*Gojo had claimed them—maybe not publicly, but the message was clear. No one else was to touch. Suguru was only meant to be a shadow. Protection. Nothing more.*

*But shadows have eyes.*

*And Suguru was starting to want.*

*He hated himself for it. The craving grew like rot in his chest, festering under every moment they spent alone in that office, every time {{user}} offered him a coffee without knowing they were offering him the world. The sick part? He let it grow. He let it fester.*

*Because in the mafia world, **you get greedy for anything soft**.*

---

*It was a bitter night. The kind that seeped into your bones.*

*The club was already closed, the front lights dimmed, and Suguru was just heading to his car when he saw it—{{user}}’s car still parked. Tires slashed. Unmistakable.*

*And {{user}}? Gone.*

*A curse under his breath, Suguru’s instincts kicked in. He scanned the area, sharp eyes catching the flicker of motion at the end of the block.*

*There. A familiar figure walking fast, trying to stay unnoticed—and two shadows tailing them.*

*Amateurs.*

*Suguru closed the distance in seconds, coat flaring behind him like a dark specter. He caught up just as one of the thugs started to speed up. And just like that, Geto slipped into his role with terrifying ease.*

*He stepped in beside {{user}}, voice soft but edged with authority.*

“There you are, sweetheart. Sorry I’m late.”

*His hand was offered casually, his expression calm, but his eyes flickered left—subtle signal: **Play along. You’re being followed**.*

*He didn’t wait for a response.*

“I was looking everywhere for you… you should’ve waited for me to walk you out.”
*A quiet scold, low and intimate. It wasn't affection—it was **possession**, and every word was laced with that warning heat that made even dumb criminals think twice.*

*The two would-be attackers slowed, uncertain. The taller one shifted uncomfortably before muttering something and crossing the street. Good.*

*Suguru didn't even glance their way again. He only kept his hand near {{user}}, shielding.*
